subject: Draft MAP: GPU pool sizing, term options & burst tolerance
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@skyline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP: GPU pool sizing, term options & burst tolerance

Evan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a sizing estimate for the dedicated GPU pool to support your evaluation workload. High-level summary:

- Evaluation phase (4 weeks): 8x A100-equivalent GPU capacity for perf benchmarks and integration tests.
- Pilot / ramp (8–12 weeks): scale to 24 GPUs as usage becomes steady; we propose a 6-month committed term for pilot pricing.
- Production baseline (12+ months): 48 GPUs with quarterly review and an annual term recommended for best-tier discounts.
- Burst tolerance: allowed bursts to 2.5x baseline for up to 48 hours per month; additional burst hours billed at the overage rate in the SOW.

Pricing options included in the attached spreadsheet: a standard committed monthly rate, a stepped discount for multi-quarter commits, and an escrow-style buffer for short-term burst capacity. I put two options in the MAP: (A) 6-month pilot commit with higher per-GPU rate and included limited burst buffer; (B) 12-month commit with lower unit price, higher included burst allowance, and a small onboarding credit.

Next steps we recommend:
- You and your infra team ratify perf target and baseline seq length by Wed (Aug 26).
- Redwood to deliver a finalized SOW and DocuSign link for the chosen option by Fri (Aug 28).
- Set a joint kickoff for the eval on Mon (Sep 6).

Attachments: MAP_v0.1.pdf, SOW_draft_20260824.docx, GPU_estimate_breakdown.xlsx

Thanks — happy to walk through line by line on a quick call.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

[Attachment stubs: MAP_v0.1.pdf (application/pdf), SOW_draft_20260824.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), GPU_estimate_breakdown.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Evan Park <evan.park@skyline.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@skyline.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@skyline.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: GPU pool sizing, term options & burst tolerance

Vivek — thanks for the detailed draft. Quick notes from our side after a short internal sync: 

- Evaluation perf target: We will validate 2k tokens/sec for our 8-shot reranker demo; confirmation by Thu (Aug 27).
- Pilot sizing: 24 GPUs looks reasonable if we can exercise burst to 3x for short windows. Your 2.5x suggestion may be tight if we run concurrent customer trials. Can Redwood support 3x bursts up to 24 hours/month for pilot?
- Term ask: Procurement prefers a 9-month initial term (rather than 6 months) to align with our QA calendar.
- Pricing: We like Option B discount curve but need clarity on overage pricing and whether quantization changes would affect support SLA.

Attached: our internal wish list and a redline on the SOW (PDF export).

Can Ben and Marissa weigh in on whether the 3x burst is feasible and how that impacts pricing? Also looping in Aisha from procurement to coordinate legal redlines.

—Evan
Evan Park
Director, Platform Engineering, Skyline AI Labs
evan.park@skyline.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199

[Attachment stub: Skyline_wishlist_and_SOW_redline.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@skyline.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: GPU pool sizing, term options & burst tolerance

Evan — appreciate the clear asks. Quick commercial options from our side: 

1) Pilot-first (9 months) — Aligns with your procurement ask. Keep pilot commit at 24 GPUs baseline; allow burst to 3x for up to 24 hours/month. Overage beyond burst billed at 1.9x unit rate. Pricing: +8% vs 12-month committed price. Includes one onboarding credit covering 40 block-hours of engineer time.

2) Annual preferred — If you can commit to 12 months, we can offer a 15% unit discount and increase included burst allowance to 36 hours/month at 2.5x, with overage at 1.6x. Also includes a one-time implementation credit and a 30% discount on quarterly eval credits.

Operational notes: allowing a 3x burst means we need an explicit buffer window in the MAP to ensure spare capacity; we typically reserve burst capacity across regional pools rather than tied to a single physical rack. That adds minimal lead time but requires a short capacity escrow.

I'll attach a simple cost delta table; Marissa, Laura — please confirm whether the overage multiplier and escrow wording are acceptable from an ops/legal perspective.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

[Attachment stub: cost_delta_pilot_vs_annual.xlsx]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Evan Park <evan.park@skyline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@skyline.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: GPU pool sizing, term options & burst tolerance

Evan / team — brief legal/ops feedback on the SOW redline: 

- Burst language: We can accept 3x bursts up to 24 hours/month for the pilot if the SOW includes (a) a per-month cap in hours, (b) a 72-hour notice window for sustained bursts >48 continuous hours, and (c) a short-run capacity escrow clause. Draft language included in the attached SOW redline.
- Overages: propose to cap overage multiplier at 2.0x for pilot (so your 1.9x is fine), with a reconciliation clause at the end of the pilot to true-up usage and potentially convert consumed burst hours into reserved capacity credit for the production term.
- Termination/rollback: add an ops rollback playbook if your team sees sustained QoS impact during burst windows.

We will incorporate these into SOW_draft_20260824.docx and send an updated DocuSign link once procurement confirms the 9-month vs 12-month ask. 

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

[Attachment stub: SOW_draft_20260827_redline.docx]

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@skyline.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Park <evan.park@skyline.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: GPU pool sizing, term options & burst tolerance

Team — procurement decision: we will move forward with the 9-month pilot (Option 1) with the following caveats: 

1) Burst: accept 3x up to 24 hours/month for the pilot. If we exceed 24 hours in any month, Skyline will notify Redwood and be billed at 1.9x for the excess hours.
2) True-up: any consumed burst hours above the included cap during pilot that exceed 120 total hours will be eligible for a reserved capacity credit if we convert to a 12-month production commitment.
3) SLA/quantization: Redwood to confirm that switching to INT8 quantization will not reduce priority support SLA; if it does, we reserve the right to revert to the previous model variant for production tests.
4) Signatures: please send final SOW and DocuSign link; procurement aims to sign within 48 hours of receiving the final doc.

Next operational items: Ben/Marissa — please update the SOW per Laura's redlines and reissue. Vivek — can we aim to have the final doc in DocuSign by Wed morning (Sep 1)?

Regards —
Aisha Rahman
Senior Procurement Manager, Skyline AI Labs
aisha.rahman@skyline.ai
